title: After 2.5 years of prompt engineering for my own campaigns, and 3 months of app building with no experience, I opened my app Mythic Scribe for Free beta testing today.
author: MythicScribeDev
selftext:
Like many others, I've been trying to use AI to play solo campaigns for years, and after a couple of years I think I've got it worked out.

It started simple in the Gemini app with 'let's play DnD', and it described a scene. I quickly realized that I didn't even know the character I was playing, so my process started with a character sheet. I worked with Gemini and we came up with a format for the sheet that would work for us both. Then it was 'Let's play DnD. Here's my character sheet.'

It took me an embarrassing amount of time to realize that the AI wasn't employing a random number generator when it "rolled dice" even as it assured me over and over again that it was. That's when 'the AI never rolls dice' rule was born. I started rolling for everything: attacks and skill checks for my characters, and attacks against my character. In the video, I roll Initiative for 4 combatants in less than 40 seconds. 

Across 2.5 years of working back and forth with Gemini refining the game master prompt that ran the game, I got tired of playing campaigns that had no story behind it, no BBEG (unless I created one by seeding the idea to the AI). So I went back to the design board with Gemini to figure out a way to create some kind of campaign structure or skeleton that I could give to the AI GM without knowing its contents so that I wouldn't know any spoilers. Together we came up with what is now the blueprint generation prompt that creates the campaign.

My GM prompt is over 7,600 words and the blueprint generation prompt is over 4,000.

The AI takes both, plus the character sheet, and builds an open-world sandbox based on the character's skills, personality, and backstory and fills it with factions, locations, NPCs, actual loot, and side quests. This all exists before you take Turn 1 in the campaign.

Once I had the prompts, I didn't know what to do with them, so I asked Gemini how difficult it would be to build an app around them and we got started on Aug 11. I used FlutterFlow + Firebase, and I literally could not have done it without Gemini. I would tell it what I wanted a page to look like, or what a function should do, and it walked me step by step through the process of building it in FlutterFlow and when I needed code for a custom function or action, or a cloud function, it spit the code out.

I would describe the app as half vibe-coded. The backend structure is mostly AI, the design, layout, and underlying prompts are mostly me.
